Stated Claim / Post Context:
How Aussies could soon be paying more at Woolworths checkouts - as the supermarket hikes prices for suppliers using its freight network

Logistic companies both in metro and regional areas have upped their fuel levies, with grocery price hikes likely on the way.

Actual Article Body:
By ASHLEY NICKEL, NEWS REPORTER, AUSTRALIA

Published:  20:15 AEST, 7 October 2026   |  Updated:  20:59 AEST, 7 October 2026

Customers are set to pay even more for their groceries as Woolworths increases its fuel levy surcharge for suppliers amid rapidly rising logistic prices.

The ongoing war in the Middle East, which has blocked major oil supply routes, has seen fuel prices continue to climb as the conflict drags on.

Logistic companies both in metro and regional areas say they have no choice but to increase their fuel levies to stay afloat.

This includes Primary Connect, which is the main supply arm of Woolworths that the supermarket giant used to transports goods from suppliers to its distribution centres and stores.

The company is also used by several other major brands including Sanitarium, PepsiCo, Ingham's and Arnott's.

Attacking President Trump is “the dumbest thing Democrats could do” should they win control of the House and Senate after the midterm elections, businessman and podcaster Patrick Bet-David argued in the latest episode of “Pod Force One.”

Bet-David, the host of the “PBD Podcast,” further predicted that if Democrats do decide to go after the president following a possible blue wave in November, the MAGA base could rally around another Trump in 2028.

“If they go and they try to arrest, impeach – the same playbook they used in 2020, 2021 – if they do that …. you know who will suddenly show up in the 2027-2028 election running for president?
